entities.name: The Protection of Information in Computer Systems

details.summary: A starting point for studying protection architectures and design principles.

entities.name: Terra: A Virtual Machine-Based Platform for Trusted Computing

details.summary: Isolated VMs and remote software identification built around a trusted VMM.

entities.name: Shielding Applications from an Untrusted Cloud with Haven

details.summary: Uses SGX to shield existing applications from an untrusted cloud platform.

entities.name: Sanctum: Minimal Hardware Extensions for Strong Software Isolation

details.summary: Combines minimal hardware extensions and a software monitor to address isolation and selected memory-access threats.

entities.name: Foreshadow: Extracting the Keys to the Intel SGX Kingdom with Transient Out-of-Order Execution

details.summary: A transient-execution attack study affecting secrets and attestation in the SGX implementations examined at publication.

entities.name: Graviton: Trusted Execution Environments on GPUs

details.summary: An architecture for trusted execution on GPUs, distinct from the AWS Graviton CPU family.

entities.name: Keystone: An Open Framework for Architecting Trusted Execution Environments

details.summary: An open framework for building customizable RISC-V trusted execution environments.
Evidence about a remote execution environment helps a verifier decide whether to entrust data to it.
Isolates selected application code and state from other software.
Extends the trusted-execution problem to accelerator code, memory, and transfers.
Connects inspectable software artifacts to evidence about software actually deployed.
A service-design category combining protected execution with attestation, key management, transparency, and routing. Implementations can have different threat models.
Adds key, storage, and access-control lifecycles for state retained across requests.
A service requirement intended to reduce selective routing of a particular user to a compromised node.

entities.name: Meta Muse Secure VM — launch architecture

details.description: Per-user VM, isolated runtime cell and privileged service separation. Provider access is not cryptographically excluded by this launch design.
details.summary: Per-user VMs, runtime isolation, and separated credential/permission services. Distinct from an operator-excluding confidential VM.

entities.name: Meta Muse Confidential VM — announced design

details.description: Separate announced capability intended to prevent provider access. General availability not established from the checked source.

entities.name: Flicker: An Execution Infrastructure for TCB Minimization

details.summary: Isolates small code fragments and supports remote verification of their execution.
details.impact: Uses TPM/DRTM mechanisms to reduce reliance on the OS.
details.limitation: TPM latency and interruption of other platform execution remain costs.

entities.name: TrustVisor: Efficient TCB Reduction and Attestation

details.summary: A small hypervisor and software micro-TPM reduce the cost of isolated execution.
details.impact: An alternative explicitly addressing performance limitations in Flicker.
details.limitation: The small monitor and underlying hardware remain trusted.

entities.name: CloudVisor: Retrofitting Protection of Virtual Machines in Multi-tenant Cloud with Nested Virtualization

details.summary: Places a small security monitor beneath the resource-managing VMM.
details.impact: Separates resource management from security protection.
details.limitation: The additional security monitor and hardware remain in the TCB.

entities.name: Komodo: Using verification to disentangle secure-enclave hardware from software

details.summary: Moves enclave management into a software monitor with machine-checkable proofs.
details.impact: An Arm TrustZone prototype accompanied by machine-checkable proofs.
details.limitation: Guarantees are bounded by verification tools, hardware assumptions, and the stated threat model.

entities.name: MI6: Secure Enclaves in a Speculative Out-of-Order Processor

details.summary: Extends Sanctum-style isolation to a speculative out-of-order processor.
details.impact: Explicitly attributes its technical extension in the abstract.
details.limitation: Exclusions include denial of service and specified hardware-fault attacks.

entities.name: Controlled-Channel Attacks: Deterministic Side Channels for Untrusted Operating Systems

details.summary: Shows how a malicious OS can extract information from memory-access patterns.
details.impact: Isolation alone does not remove observable execution patterns.
details.limitation: Claims are limited to the targets and attacker assumptions in the original work.

entities.name: Slalom: Fast, Verifiable and Private Execution of Neural Networks in Trusted Hardware

details.summary: Delegates selected DNN computation from a TEE to an untrusted GPU.
details.impact: A different design direction from making the GPU itself a TEE.
details.limitation: Supported operations and the conditions for verifiability and privacy must be distinguished.
